evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check only requires positive, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. It never checks that the manager before/after snapshots share a nonempty boot ID. The separate boot_id_changed check at lines 1117-1124 applies only to the reboot snapshots. Therefore an intervening guest reboot can change both the manager PID and invocation ID and be falsely accepted as an isolated manager restart. Requiring equal nonempty boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair while retaining the PID/invocation checks is a routine correctness repair of the existing verification behavior, not a new contract requirement or owner-level change.
